headline: Execution expected to ramp up from H2FY27E onwards.

highlights: Gross margins contracted by 231bps YoY (+240bps QoQ) to 32.1% in Q2FY27.
EBITDA stood at INR 917mn (- 72.1% YoY/-63.5% QoQ), below our estimates of INR 2,826mn.

EBITDA margin contracted by 752bps YoY (-594bps QoQ) to 3.5% in Q2FY27, due to fixed-cost under-absorption, partially offset by lower manpower costs but pressured by higher energy, transport, logistics and provisioning costs.
PAT stood at INR 411mn (-60.9% YoY/+35.5% QoQ) in Q2FY27; in line with our estimates of INR 413mn.
valuation: Outlook & Valuation: Afcons Infrastructure enters H2FY27 with improving execution visibility and expects H2FY27 to be meaningfully stronger than H1FY27, as land handovers, approvals, and both Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train TBMs unlock work fronts, though formal FY27E revenue and margin guidance remains withheld due to energy availability constraints in Bangladesh and West Asia geopolitical uncertainty.
The stock is trading at an EV/EBITDA of 11.7x based on FY27E EBITDA.

At the CMP of INR 219 per share, we maintain our “BUY” rating at a TP of INR 353 per share; valued at an EV/EBITDA of 7x (~50% discount to the 1-year forward mean EV/EBITDA of 15.5x) and its FY29E EBITDA of INR 12,931mn; an upside of 61.2%.
watch: Key Highlights Order Book visibility underpins FY28E growth: Afcons Infrastructure enters H2FY27 with an order book of ~INR 438.36bn (excluding L1) and YTD FY27 intake of ~INR 194.37bn, tracking firmly toward the INR 300bn inflow guidance backed by an ~INR 800bn pipeline for the year.
Key risks are stretched government payments, UP Jal Jeevan Mission execution (INR 3.72bn outstanding), Vadhvan Port approval delays, and West Asia geopolitical disruption.
